D22·3gbx — 2026-10-10
chose: Each assignment is a new event, `lane_assigned {run, lane: integer ≥1, task?}` on envelope session cli: with task, the coordinator gave that lane that task; without, it freed the lane (a launch that resolved to no session files no handoff to free it). The fold keeps `run.assignments` [{lane, task, ts}], lane order, present only when non-empty: an assignment replaces the lane's and any other lane's hold on the same task, and ends at the handoff for its task, at run_stopped and at run_adopted (the old driver's lanes are gone). Excluded from drift like every driver event (commit-attribution D18). Where the record shows "the task in flight", a lanes run shows what its lanes hold, `L<k> <task>` joined by ", ": describeRun (the injected Driven line and sofar status), the statusline's drive segment, the prompt's drive line and the progress file's `task`.
over: Recording lanes only in the progress file (not the record, invisible to other clones and to the injected digest); a separate lane_released event type; putting the lane on handoff (an unresolved launch files no handoff, so the lane would read held forever)
because: The task asks that the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task; both read the fold, so the assignment has to be an event. One event with an optional task is the smallest schema that can also free a lane after an unresolved launch.
